tasks.title: Parallel sum: scope and chunks
tasks.statement: par_sum(v: &[i64], parts: usize) → i64: cut the slice into parts pieces (the last may be shorter; parts ≥ 1), start one thread per piece in thread::scope, let each compute its own sum, then add the results. The data is not copied: the threads take references to the pieces.
tasks.hint: chunks(size) gives slices; s.spawn(move || …) in a scope can take a slice directly; h.join().unwrap() returns the sum of the piece.

tasks.title: spawn and join: results in order
tasks.statement: squares_in_threads(n) → Vec<u64>: for each i from 1 to n start a thread that returns i², and collect the results IN THE ORDER of i (wait for the threads one by one through JoinHandle). word_lengths(words: Vec<String>) → Vec<usize> — each word is processed in its own thread (the words move into the threads).
tasks.hint: First start ALL the threads (collect the handles into a vector), only then join: otherwise the threads run one after another.

tasks.title: Fix: the closure borrows a local
tasks.statement: sum_in_thread starts a thread that sums a vector, but the closure takes v by reference, and the thread may outlive the function (E0373). Fix it with one word.
tasks.hint: move hands the vector over to the thread completely.

tasks.title: Fix: Rc is not Send
tasks.statement: len_in_thread wraps a string in an Rc and sends it to a thread — the compiler refuses (Rc does not implement Send). Replace Rc with Arc and leave the rest as is.
tasks.hint: Arc has the same methods new, clone and strong_count — put it in place of Rc and import std::sync::Arc.

tasks.title: Shared counter: Arc<Mutex<u64>>
tasks.statement: count_parallel(threads: usize, per_thread: u64) → u64: start threads threads, each increasing the shared counter (Arc<Mutex<u64>>) by one per_thread times; return the total. contended(threads, per_thread) → u64 — the same, but each thread first counts locally and adds to the shared one once.
tasks.hint: Each thread gets its own clone of the Arc; the lock is taken for a single operation: *c.lock().unwrap() += 1.

tasks.title: Transfers without deadlocks
tasks.statement: transfer_all(accounts: &[Arc<Mutex<i64>>], transfers: &[(usize, usize, i64)]) → Vec<i64>: each transfer (from, to, amount) runs in its own thread at the same time as the others. To avoid a deadlock, always lock the accounts in order of increasing index. from == to — do nothing. Return the final balances (negative ones are allowed).
tasks.hint: Always lock the account with the smaller index first: then a wait cycle is impossible.

tasks.title: A cache on RwLock
tasks.statement: Cache holds a RwLock<HashMap<u64, u64>> and an AtomicUsize with the number of real computations. get(&self, x, f: fn(u64) → u64) → u64: reads under the read lock; if the value is missing, takes the write lock, checks again and computes (the computation is counted). computations(&self) → usize. When called from several threads, one value must be computed exactly once.
tasks.hint: After getting the write lock, check the key again: while you waited, another thread may have computed it.

tasks.title: Parallel word count
tasks.statement: word_count_par(text: &str, parts: usize) → BTreeMap<String, usize>: divide the lines of the text among parts threads (in order, in blocks), each counts words (lowercase; words are letters and digits) in its own HashMap, then merge the results. The result must not depend on parts.
tasks.hint: Each thread returns its own HashMap; the overall result is assembled in the main thread — without locks.

tasks.title: par_map: parallel transformation
tasks.statement: par_map<T, U, F>(v: &[T], parts: usize, f: F) → Vec<U> where T: Sync, U: Send, F: Fn(&T) → U + Sync: apply f to all elements, splitting the slice into parts pieces across threads; the result is in the original order.
tasks.hint: The closure f is called from several threads through a shared reference: that is why F: Sync; take &f and copy the reference into the threads.

tasks.title: A pipeline of threads and channels
tasks.statement: pipeline(n: u64) → Vec<u64>: three stages in three threads, connected by mpsc channels: (1) a generator sends the numbers 1..=n; (2) squares them; (3) a filter keeps the squares divisible by 3. The main thread collects the result (the order is preserved).
tasks.hint: Each stage owns its tx; when a stage is finished, its tx is closed — the next stage leaves its loop over rx.

tasks.title: Several producers, one receiver
tasks.statement: fan_in(producers: usize, items: usize) → Vec<(usize, usize)>: start producers threads; thread p sends the pairs (p, 0), (p, 1), …, (p, items-1) into a shared channel. The main thread collects ALL the messages and returns them sorted. To do this, clone the sender and do not forget to close the original.
tasks.hint: drop(tx) in the main thread closes the original sender: otherwise rx.iter() never ends.

tasks.title: Ping-pong over two channels
tasks.statement: ping_pong(rounds: u32) → Vec<String>: two threads exchange messages over two channels: «ping» from the first to the second, «pong» back, rounds times. Each thread records events in a shared log (a separate channel or a value returned from join) in the order «ping 1», «pong 1», «ping 2», …
tasks.hint: Ping waits for the reply with recv() after every send(): that lines the events up strictly in turn.

tasks.title: Bounded channel: back pressure
tasks.statement: bounded_sum(items: u64, capacity: usize) → (u64, bool): a producer in a thread sends the numbers 1..=items into sync_channel(capacity); the consumer in the main thread sums them. The second value is true if the consumer received the numbers strictly in order 1, 2, 3, …
tasks.hint: sync_channel(0) is a rendezvous: send waits until the receiver takes the value.

tasks.title: A bounded queue on Mutex and Condvar
tasks.statement: BoundedQueue<T> { Mutex<VecDeque<T>>, Condvar not_empty, Condvar not_full, capacity }: push(&self, x) waits until there is room; pop(&self) → T waits until an element appears. Check: producers and consumers in different threads, the sum of all elements matches.
tasks.hint: Always wait for a condition in a while loop: after waking up, the condition must be checked again.

tasks.title: Barrier: two phases
tasks.statement: phases(n: usize) → Vec<u64>: n threads; in phase 1, thread i writes the value (i+1)² into slot i of a shared vector; after a Barrier, in phase 2, each thread reads the sum of all slots and returns it. Thanks to the barrier, all n results are the same.
tasks.hint: barrier.wait() blocks the thread until all n arrive; only after it is it safe to read the other slots.

tasks.title: Atomics: fetch_add and fetch_max
tasks.statement: atomic_stats(threads: usize, per_thread: usize) → (usize, usize, usize). The thread with number id (0..threads): increases the shared counter hits per_thread times (fetch_add); writes its id into biggest through fetch_max; tries to claim the flag first through compare_exchange(0, id + 1) — exactly one thread succeeds. Return (hits, the largest id, the number of threads that claimed the flag).
tasks.hint: compare_exchange(0, id+1, …) succeeds for exactly one thread — there is one winner regardless of the start order.

tasks.title: A spinlock on AtomicBool
tasks.statement: SpinLock { locked: AtomicBool }: lock(&self) spins until compare_exchange(false, true, Acquire, Relaxed) succeeds (std::hint::spin_loop() in the loop); unlock(&self) writes false (Release). The driver checks that no more than one thread is inside the critical section at a time.
tasks.hint: A successful compare_exchange(false, true) means «I took the lock»; Acquire when taking and Release when releasing link the sections.

tasks.title: Run exactly once
tasks.statement: Once { done: AtomicBool }: run(&self, f: impl FnOnce()) → bool: runs f only if nobody has started yet (compare_exchange on the flag); returns true to the one who ran it. The driver starts 16 threads: f must fire exactly once.
tasks.hint: Only one compare_exchange(false, true) will succeed — and that thread calls f.

tasks.title: Your own thread pool
tasks.statement: ThreadPool::new(n) starts n workers; execute(&self, job: impl FnOnce() + Send + 'static) puts a job into the channel; shutdown(self) closes the channel and waits for the workers (all the queued jobs are done). The workers take jobs from a shared Arc<Mutex<Receiver<Job>>>.
tasks.hint: The worker: loop { let job = rx.lock().unwrap().recv(); … } — the lock is held only for the duration of recv; a closed channel → Err → we exit.

tasks.title: chunks_mut: change in place in parallel
tasks.statement: par_scale(v: &mut [i64], k: i64, parts: usize): multiply every element by k, splitting the slice into parts non-overlapping mutable pieces (chunks_mut) and starting a thread for each. par_prefix_marks(v: &mut [i64]) — replace every element with its index × value (the threads get the offset of their piece).
tasks.hint: chunks_mut gives non-overlapping &mut [T]: each piece can be handed to its own thread without locks.

tasks.title: Primes: segments across threads
tasks.statement: count_primes(n: u64, parts: usize) → usize: how many primes are below n. The range 2..n is divided into parts segments; each thread checks the numbers of its segment by trial division. The result does not depend on parts. For n up to 200 000 the work must fit within the limit.
tasks.hint: Segment [lo, hi): lo = 2 + p·size, hi = min(lo + size, n); the thread returns the number of primes in it.

tasks.title: Matrix: rows across threads
tasks.statement: matmul(a: &[Vec<i64>], b: &[Vec<i64>]) → Vec<Vec<i64>>: the product of matrices (the sizes are compatible). Each row of the result is computed in a separate thread inside a scope; the result must match the sequential computation.
tasks.hint: Each row of the result depends only on a row of a and the whole of b — the threads do not overlap; b is taken by a shared reference.

tasks.title: Parallel merge sort
tasks.statement: par_sort(v: Vec<i64>) → Vec<i64>: merge sort; the halves are sorted in different threads (thread::scope) while the length is greater than 1000, below that the ordinary sort. The result matches v.sort().
tasks.hint: The thread gets the whole right half (split_off), the left one is sorted in the current thread; then merge the two sorted vectors.

tasks.title: Histogram: each thread has its own copy
tasks.statement: histogram(data: &[u8], parts: usize) → [usize; 16]: the frequency of the values data[i] % 16. Each thread fills ITS OWN array [usize; 16] over its piece, then the arrays are added up. No shared counters inside the loop.
tasks.hint: The array [usize; 16] is a Copy type, so it is easy to return from a thread; add up element by element.

tasks.title: A poisoned mutex
tasks.statement: poison_demo() → (bool, i32, bool): create an Arc<Mutex<i32>> with the value 10; a thread takes the lock, adds 5 and panics; then: (1) is_poisoned() of the lock, (2) the value obtained through lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()), (3) whether an ordinary lock().is_ok() succeeds after clear_poison().
tasks.hint: PoisonError::into_inner hands out the guard even for a poisoned mutex; clear_poison removes the mark.

tasks.title: try_lock: without waiting
tasks.statement: try_lock_demo() → Vec<bool>: a lock Mutex<i32>. Record is_ok() of this sequence: try_lock() on a free one; on a taken one (the guard is alive in this very thread) — in another thread through scope; in this thread after the release; then RwLock: try_write() while a reader is alive; try_read() while a reader is alive.
tasks.hint: try_lock returns Err(WouldBlock) if the lock is taken; a live guard is a variable, not a call expression.

tasks.title: Cancelling a thread with a flag
tasks.statement: cancel_demo() → (bool, bool): a worker in a loop increases a shared AtomicU64 and checks an Arc<AtomicBool> «stop». The main thread waits until the counter is ≥ 1000, sets stop, and joins the worker. Return (the thread finished, the counter at the moment of join is ≥ 1000).
tasks.hint: The cancellation flag is an AtomicBool in an Arc: the worker reads it in the loop, the main thread later sets it to true.

tasks.title: The Send and 'static bounds
tasks.statement: run_in_thread<R, F>(f: F) → R runs a closure in a new thread and returns the result (join). Write the correct bounds: F: FnOnce() → R + Send + 'static, R: Send + 'static. run_all<R, F>(jobs: Vec<F>) → Vec<R> runs all of them in parallel and returns the results in order.
tasks.hint: thread::spawn requires Send + 'static from the closure and Send + 'static from the result — repeat these bounds in the where clause.

tasks.title: Named threads and thread_local
tasks.statement: named_work(n: usize) → Vec<(String, u32)>: start n threads through thread::Builder with the names «worker-0», «worker-1», …; in each, a thread_local counter (Cell<u32>) is increased (i+1) times; the thread returns (its name through thread::current().name(), the value of the local counter). The results are in the order of starting.
tasks.hint: thread_local gives each thread its own copy: changes in the workers are not visible to the main thread.

tasks.title: Dining philosophers
tasks.statement: philosophers(n: usize, meals: usize) → Vec<usize>: n philosophers at a round table, n forks (Mutex<()>). Philosopher i takes forks i and (i+1)%n — BUT always the one with the smaller number first, so there is no deadlock. Each «eats» meals times (increases their own counter). Return the number of meals of each.
tasks.hint: The fork with the smaller number first — all philosophers line up their acquisition in the same order, there is no wait cycle; with n = 1 both forks coincide.
